      parent = item.parentElement;
      while (parent) {
        var style = getComputedStyle(parent);
        if (style.overflowY === 'auto' || style.overflowY === 'scroll') break;
        parent = parent.parentElement;
      }
    }
    if (!parent) return;

    var parentRect = parent.getBoundingClientRect();
    var itemRect = item.getBoundingClientRect();
    if (itemRect.top >= parentRect.top && itemRect.bottom <= parentRect.bottom) return;

    var itemTopRelative = itemRect.top - parentRect.top + parent.scrollTop;
    parent.scrollTop = itemTopRelative - parentRect.height / 2 + itemRect.height / 2;
  } catch (e) {}
})();</script></div></div></div></div></div></nav><main id="content-container" class="lg:flex-1 lg:min-w-0"><script type="application/ld+json">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@graph":[{"@type":"Organization","@id":"https://code.claude.com/#organization","name":"Claude Code Docs","url":"https://code.claude.com","logo":{"@type":"ImageObject","url":"https://mintcdn.com/claude-code/c5r9_6tjPMzFdDDT/logo/light.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=c5r9_6tjPMzFdDDT&q=85&s=78fd01ff4f4340295a4f66e2ea54903c"}},{"@type":"WebSite","@id":"https://code.claude.com/docs#website","name":"Claude Code Docs","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs","publisher":{"@id":"https://code.claude.com/#organization"}},{"@type":"WebPage","@id":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide#webpage","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide","name":"Automate actions with hooks","description":"Run shell commands automatically when Claude Code edits files, finishes tasks, or needs input. /* ============================================================
   Collapsible right table of contents (toggled by toc-collapse.js)
   ============================================================ */

/* Dimensions mirrored from Mintlify's compiled mint-theme layout. If a
   Mintlify update moves the button or the collapsed reading column,
   re-measure these on a rendered page. */
:root {
  --toc-wrapper-max: 92rem; /* centered layout wrapper max-width */
  --toc-wrapper-pad: 2rem; /* wrapper right padding */
  --toc-col: 19rem; /* ToC column width, incl. its 2.5rem left padding */
  --toc-side: 28rem; /* side column space #content-area reserves */
  --toc-btn-size: 1.75rem; /* ours, not mirrored: the toggle's diameter */
}

/* Hidden by default: below the xl breakpoint Mintlify hides the ToC
   anyway, and pages that render no ToC (wide-mode pages) get no toggle. */
#toc-collapse-toggle {
  display: none;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  position: fixed;
  top: 10rem;
  /* Sits just left of the ToC column, inside its 2.5rem left-padding
     strip: at the column's left edge, minus the button's own width and
     a small gap. 100% rather than 100vw so a classic scrollbar doesn't
     shift the math (percentages on fixed elements resolve against the
     layout viewport). */
  right: calc(
    max((100% - var(--toc-wrapper-max)) / 2, 0px) + var(--toc-wrapper-pad) +
      var(--toc-col) - var(--toc-btn-size) - 0.35rem
  );
  transition: right 200ms ease-out;
  z-index: 30;
  width: var(--toc-btn-size);
  height: var(--toc-btn-size);
  border-radius: 9999px;
  border: 1px solid hsl(var(--border-300) / 0.15);
  background: hsl(var(--bg-100));
  color: hsl(var(--text-400));
  cursor: pointer;
}

#toc-collapse-toggle:hover {
  background: hsl(var(--bg-300));
  color: hsl(var(--text-100));
}

#toc-collapse-toggle svg {
  width: 14px;
  height: 14px;
  fill: none;
  stroke: currentColor;
  stroke-width: 2.5;
  stroke-linecap: round;
  stroke-linejoin: round;
}

/* The list glyph only appears while the button is parked at the right
   edge, so the collapsed control still reads as the table of contents. */
#toc-collapse-toggle .toc-glyph {
  display: none;
  stroke-width: 2;
}

/* A fixed-position button would repeat on every printed page. */
@media print {
  #toc-collapse-toggle {
    display: none !important;
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  #toc-collapse-toggle {
    transition: none;
  }
}

@media (min-width: 1280px) {
  html:has(#table-of-contents-layout) #toc-collapse-toggle {
    display: flex;
  }

  html.toc-collapsed #toc-collapse-toggle .toc-chevron {
    transform: rotate(180deg);
  }

  /* The column is gone while collapsed, so the button moves to the
     right edge where the restored ToC will reappear, widening into a
     pill that pairs the chevron with the list glyph. */
  html.toc-collapsed #toc-collapse-toggle {
    right: 0.5rem;
    width: auto;
    padding: 0 0.5rem;
    gap: 0.25rem;
  }

  html.toc-collapsed #toc-collapse-toggle .toc-glyph {
    display: block;
  }

  html.toc-collapsed #table-of-contents-layout {
    display: none !important;
  }

  /* Also hide the side column's wrapper: left in flow at zero width,
     it keeps its 3rem flex gap as dead space at the right edge. Scoped
     with :has() so the wrapper is untouched when it holds other
     content, such as the open assistant panel. */
  html.toc-collapsed #content-side-layout:has(#table-of-contents-layout) {
    display: none !important;
  }

  /* Mintlify sizes the content column assuming the side column is
     present (xl:w-[calc(100%-28rem)]); reclaim that space when collapsed.
     Scoped with :has() so pages that render no ToC, such as wide-mode
     pages, keep their own layout. Written out twice rather than nested:
     CSS nesting shipped later than :has(), so nesting here would break
     the cap in browsers that pass the :has() support guard. */
  html.toc-collapsed #content-container:has(#table-of-contents-layout) #content-area {
    width: 100% !important;
  }

  /* Safety bound on the widened reading column. The centered wrapper
     already caps overall width, so today this only bites at the
     wrapper's max, where it equals the natural content width; it exists
     so line length can't run away if the wrapper cap ever changes. */
  html.toc-collapsed #content-container:has(#table-of-contents-layout) #content-area > * {
    max-width: calc(var(--toc-wrapper-max) - var(--toc-side));
  }
}

class="mdx-content @container/columns-container relative mt-8 prose prose-gray dark:prose-invert [contain:inline-size] isolate empty:hidden mb-14" data-page-title="Automate actions with hooks" data-page-href="/en/hooks-guide" id="content"><span data-as="p">Hooks are user-defined shell commands. Claude Code runs them at specific points in its lifecycle, which gives you deterministic control: certain actions always happen rather than relying on the LLM to choose to run them. Use hooks to enforce project rules, automate repetitive tasks, and integrate Claude Code with your existing tools.</span>
<span data-as="p">For decisions that require judgment rather than deterministic rules, you can also use <a href="#prompt-based-hooks" class="link">prompt-based hooks</a> or <a href="#agent-based-hooks" class="link">agent-based hooks</a> that use a Claude model to evaluate conditions.</span>
<span data-as="p">For other ways to extend Claude Code, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/skills">skills</a> for giving Claude additional instructions and executable commands, <a class="link" href="/docs/en/sub-agents">subagents</a> for running tasks in isolated contexts, and <a class="link" href="/docs/en/plugins">plugins</a> for packaging extensions to share across projects.</span>

<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="what-you-can-automate"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#what-you-can-automate" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">What you can automate</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Hooks let you run code at key points in Claude Code’s lifecycle: format files after edits, block commands before they execute, send notifications when Claude needs input, inject context at session start, and more. For the full list of hook events, see the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#hook-lifecycle">Hooks reference</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">Each example includes a ready-to-use configuration block that you add to a <a href="#configure-hook-location" class="link">settings file</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">For a production example of hooks that run a separate model review and feed findings back into the session, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/security-guidance#how-the-plugin-integrates-with-claude-code">how the <code>security-guidance</code> plugin integrates with Claude Code</a>.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="get-notified-when-claude-needs-input"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#get-notified-when-claude-needs-input" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Get notified when Claude needs input</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Get a desktop notification whenever Claude finishes working and needs your input, so you can switch to other tasks without checking the terminal.</span>
<span data-as="p">This hook uses the <code>Notification</code> event, which Claude Code fires when Claude is waiting for input or permission. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#notification">when each notification type fires</a> for the exact timing. Each tab below uses the platform’s native notification command. Add this to <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code>:</span>

Test the command directly in PowerShell first. If you run Claude Code inside WSL, <code>powershell.exe</code> must be available on your <code>PATH</code> through Windows interop.</span></div></details></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">The empty <code>matcher</code> fires on all notification types. To fire only on specific events, set it to one of these values:</span>

<span data-as="p">Claude Code times <code>permission_prompt</code> differently in a terminal and in Claude Desktop, the VS Code extension, and other hosts that answer permission requests through the Agent SDK. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#notification">when each notification type fires</a> for both timings.</span>
<span data-as="p">The <code>agent_needs_input</code> and <code>agent_completed</code> matchers require Claude Code v2.1.198 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p">The <code>quota_auto_resume_fired</code>, <code>quota_auto_resume_stale</code>, and <code>quota_auto_resume_disabled</code> matchers require Claude Code v2.1.234 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p">In terminal sessions, <code>permission_prompt</code> for a sandboxed command’s network request requires Claude Code v2.1.246 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p"><code>agent_needs_input</code> for a teammate’s terminal setup question requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later.</span>
<span data-as="p">Type <code>/hooks</code> and select <code>Notification</code> to confirm the hook is registered. For the full event schema, see the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#notification">Notification reference</a>.</span>

<span data-as="p">Automatically run <a href="https://prettier.io/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" class="link">Prettier</a> on every file Claude edits, so formatting stays consistent without manual intervention.</span>
<span data-as="p">This hook uses the <code>PostToolUse</code> event with an <code>Edit|Write</code> matcher, so it runs only after file-editing tools. The command extracts the edited file path with <a href="https://jqlang.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" class="link"><code>jq</code></a> and passes it to Prettier. Add this to <code>.claude/settings.json</code> in your project root:</span>

<span data-as="p">To test the hook, ask Claude to add a line with single-quoted strings to a JavaScript file, then open the file: with Prettier’s default settings, the hook rewrites them to double quotes.</span>
<span data-as="p">When the hook succeeds, Claude Code shows nothing in the conversation. To confirm the hook ran, check that the edited file is reformatted, or see <a href="#debug-techniques" class="link">Debug techniques</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">To reformat a specific file however it changes, including when a <code>Bash</code> command rewrites it, use a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#filechanged">FileChanged</a> hook instead.</span>
<div role="note" aria-label="Note" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-blue-200 bg-blue-50 dark:border-blue-900 dark:bg-blue-600/20" data-callout-type="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-4 text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300"><path d="M 9 1.6714 C 13.0371 1.6714 16.3286 4.9629 16.3286 9 C 16.3286 13.0371 13.0371 16.3286 9 16.3286 C 7.0574 16.3252 5.1953 15.552 3.8217 14.1783 C 2.448 12.8047 1.6748 10.9426 1.6714 9 C 1.6714 4.9629 4.9629 1.6714 9 1.6714 Z M 9 0 C 4.0371 0 0 4.0371 0 9 C 0 13.9629 4.0371 18 9 18 C 13.9629 18 18 13.9629 18 9 C 18 4.0371 13.9629 0 9 0 Z M 10.2857 3.8571 H 7.7143 V 10.2857 H 10.2857 V 3.8571 Z M 10.2857 11.5714 H 7.7143 V 14.1429 H 10.2857 V 11.5714 Z" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" fill-rule="evenodd" clip-rule="evenodd"></path></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">The Bash examples on this page use <code>jq</code> for JSON parsing. <h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="block-edits-to-protected-files"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#block-edits-to-protected-files" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Block edits to protected files</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Prevent Claude from modifying sensitive files like <code>.env</code>, <code>package-lock.json</code>, or anything in <code>.git/</code>. Claude receives feedback explaining why the edit was blocked, so it can adjust its approach.</span>
<span data-as="p">This example uses a separate script file that the hook calls. The script checks the target file path against a list of protected patterns and exits with code 2 to block the edit.</span>

<span data-as="p">Track when settings or skills files change during a session. The <code>ConfigChange</code> event fires when an external process or editor modifies a configuration file, so you can log changes for compliance or block unauthorized modifications.</span>
<span data-as="p">This example appends each change to an audit log. Add this to <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code>:</span>

<span data-as="p">The matcher filters by configuration type: <code>user_settings</code>, <code>project_settings</code>, <code>local_settings</code>, <code>policy_settings</code>, or <code>skills</code>. To block a change from taking effect, exit with code 2 or return <code>{&quot;decision&quot;: &quot;block&quot;}</code>. See the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#configchange">ConfigChange reference</a> for the full input schema.</span>
<span data-as="p">To confirm the hook records changes, edit a settings file in another editor while a session is running, then open <code>~/claude-config-audit.log</code>: the hook appends one JSON line per change with the timestamp, source, and file path.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="reload-environment-when-directory-or-files-change"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#reload-environment-when-directory-or-files-change" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Reload environment when directory or files change</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Some projects set different environment variables depending on which directory you are in. Tools like <a href="https://direnv.net/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" class="link">direnv</a> do this automatically in your shell, but Claude’s Bash tool doesn’t pick up those changes on its own.</span>
<span data-as="p">Pairing a <code>SessionStart</code> hook with a <code>CwdChanged</code> hook fixes this. <code>SessionStart</code> loads the variables for the directory you launch in, and <code>CwdChanged</code> reloads them each time Claude changes directory. Both write to <code>CLAUDE_ENV_FILE</code>, which Claude Code runs as a script preamble before each Bash command. Add this to <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code>:</span>

<span data-as="p">Run <code>direnv allow</code> once in each directory that has an <code>.envrc</code> so direnv is permitted to load it. If you use devbox or nix instead of direnv, the same pattern works with <code>devbox shellenv</code> or <code>devbox global shellenv</code> in place of <code>direnv export bash</code>.</span>
<span data-as="p">To react to specific files instead of every directory change, use <code>FileChanged</code> with a <code>matcher</code> listing the filenames to watch, separated by <code>|</code>. When building the watch list, Claude Code splits this value into literal filenames rather than evaluating it as a regex. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#filechanged">FileChanged</a> for how the same value also filters which hook groups run when a file changes. This example watches <code>.envrc</code> and <code>.env</code> in the working directory:</span>

<span data-as="p">Skip the approval dialog for tool calls you always allow. This example auto-approves <code>ExitPlanMode</code>, the tool Claude calls when it finishes presenting a plan and asks to proceed, so you aren’t prompted every time a plan is ready.</span>
<span data-as="p">Unlike the exit-code examples above, auto-approval requires your hook to write a JSON decision to stdout. Claude Code runs <code>PermissionRequest</code> hooks when it’s about to ask you for permission, and if your hook returns <code>&quot;behavior&quot;: &quot;allow&quot;</code>, Claude Code answers the request on your behalf.</span>
<span data-as="p">The matcher scopes the hook to <code>ExitPlanMode</code> only, so no other prompts are affected. Add this to <code>~/.claude/settings.json</code>:</span>

<span data-as="p">When the hook approves, Claude Code exits plan mode and restores whatever permission mode was active before you entered plan mode. The transcript shows “Allowed by PermissionRequest hook” where the dialog would have appeared. The hook path always keeps the current conversation: it can’t clear context and start a fresh implementation session the way the dialog can.</span>
<span data-as="p">To set a specific permission mode instead, your hook’s output can include an <code>updatedPermissions</code> array with a <code>setMode</code> entry. The <code>mode</code> value is any permission mode like <code>default</code>, <code>acceptEdits</code>, or <code>bypassPermissions</code>, and <code>destination: &quot;session&quot;</code> applies it for the current session only.</span>

[&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p"><code>bypassPermissions</code> only applies if the session was launched with bypass mode already available: <code>--dangerously-skip-permissions</code>, <code>--permission-mode bypassPermissions</code>, <code>--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions</code>, or <code>permissions.defaultMode: &quot;bypassPermissions&quot;</code> in settings, and not disabled by <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions#managed-settings"><code>permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode</code></a> or by starting the session in <a class="link" href="/docs/en/cli-reference#cli-flags">restricted mode</a>. It is never persisted as <code>defaultMode</code>.</span></div></div>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">        { </span><span style="color:#116329;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">&quot;type&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: </span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">&quot;setMode&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">, </span><span style="color:#116329;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">&quot;mode&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: </span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">&quot;acceptEdits&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">, </span><span style="color:#116329;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">&quot;destination&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: </span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">&quot;session&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4"> }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">      ]</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">    }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">  }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">}</span></span>
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div class="code-block-fade-overlay print:hidden" data-fade-overlay="true" aria-hidden="true" style="--fade-color-light:#ffffff;--fade-color-dark:#0B0C0E"></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Keep the matcher as narrow as possible. Matching on <code>.*</code> or leaving the matcher empty would auto-approve every tool permission prompt, including file writes and shell commands. See the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#permissionrequest-decision-control">PermissionRequest reference</a> for the full set of decision fields.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="how-hooks-work"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#how-hooks-work" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">How hooks work</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Claude Code fires hook events at specific points in its lifecycle. When an event fires, Claude Code runs all matching hooks in parallel; see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#hook-handler-fields">Hook handler fields</a> for how duplicate handlers are treated. The table below shows each event and when it triggers:</span>

Useful for reactive environment management with tools like direnv</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>DirectoryAdded</code></td><td style="text-align:left">When a working directory is added mid-session via <code>/add-dir</code> or the SDK <code>register_repo_root</code> control request</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>FileChanged</code></td><td style="text-align:left">When a watched file changes on disk. Can block the switch</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>PostModelSwitch</code></td><td style="text-align:left">After the session’s model changes, including changes Claude Code makes on its own, such as restoring the model when you resume a session</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>Elicitation</code></td><td style="text-align:left">When an MCP server requests user input during a tool call</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>ElicitationResult</code></td><td style="text-align:left">After a user responds to an MCP elicitation, before the response is sent back to the server</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>SessionEnd</code></td><td style="text-align:left">When a session terminates</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Each hook has a <code>type</code> that determines how it runs. Most hooks use <code>&quot;type&quot;: &quot;command&quot;</code>, which runs a shell command. Four other types are available:</span>
<ul>
<li><code>&quot;type&quot;: &quot;http&quot;</code>: POST event data to a URL. See <a href="#http-hooks" class="link">HTTP hooks</a>.</li>
<li><code>&quot;type&quot;: &quot;mcp_tool&quot;</code>: call a tool on an already-connected MCP server. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#mcp-tool-hook-fields">MCP tool hooks</a>.</li>
<li><code>&quot;type&quot;: &quot;prompt&quot;</code>: single-turn LLM evaluation. See <a href="#prompt-based-hooks" class="link">Prompt-based hooks</a>.</li>
<li><code>&quot;type&quot;: &quot;agent&quot;</code>: multi-turn verification with tool access. Agent hooks are experimental and may change. See <a href="#agent-based-hooks" class="link">Agent-based hooks</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="combine-results-from-multiple-hooks"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#combine-results-from-multiple-hooks" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Combine results from multiple hooks</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">When multiple hooks match the same event, every hook’s command runs to completion before Claude Code merges the results. One hook returning <code>deny</code> doesn’t stop sibling hooks from executing. Don’t rely on one hook’s <code>deny</code> to suppress side effects in another hook.</span>
<span data-as="p">After all matching hooks finish, Claude Code combines their outputs. For <code>PreToolUse</code> permission decisions, the most restrictive answer applies, in the order <code>deny</code>, <code>defer</code>, <code>ask</code>, <code>allow</code>. Text from <code>additionalContext</code> is kept from every hook and passed to Claude together.</span>
<span data-as="p">The example below registers two <code>PreToolUse</code> hooks on <code>Bash</code>. The first appends every command to a log file and exits 0. The second runs a script that exits 2 to deny when the command contains <code>rm -rf</code>:</span>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">          },</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">          {</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#116329;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">            &quot;type&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: </span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">&quot;command&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">,</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#116329;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">            &quot;command&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: </span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">&quot;</span><span style="color:#CF222E;--shiki-dark:#D7BA7D">\&quot;</span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR</span><span style="color:#CF222E;--shiki-dark:#D7BA7D">\&quot;</span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">/.claude/hooks/block-rm-rf.sh&quot;</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">          }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">        ]</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">      }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">    ]</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">  }</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">}</span></span>
</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div class="code-block-fade-overlay print:hidden" data-fade-overlay="true" aria-hidden="true" style="--fade-color-light:#ffffff;--fade-color-dark:#0B0C0E"></div></div>
<span data-as="p">When Claude tries to run <code>rm -rf /tmp/build</code>, both hooks execute in parallel. The logging hook writes the command to <code>~/.claude/bash.log</code> and exits 0, which reports no decision. The guardrail hook exits 2, which denies the tool call. The deny takes precedence, so Claude Code blocks the command and shows Claude the guardrail’s stderr. The log entry is still written because the logging hook already ran.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="read-input-and-return-output"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#read-input-and-return-output" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Read input and return output</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Hooks communicate with Claude Code through stdin, stdout, stderr, and exit codes. When an event fires, Claude Code passes event-specific data as JSON to your script’s stdin. Your script reads that data, does its work, and tells Claude Code what to do next via the exit code.</span>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="hook-input"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#hook-input" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Hook input</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">Every event includes common fields like <code>session_id</code>, a unique ID for the session, and <code>cwd</code>, the working directory when the event fired, but each event type adds different data. When Claude runs a Bash command, a <code>PreToolUse</code> hook receives these fields on stdin:</span>
<ul>
<li><code>hook_event_name</code>: the event that triggered the hook</li>
<li><code>tool_name</code>: the tool Claude is about to use</li>
<li><code>tool_input</code>: the arguments Claude passed to the tool. For Bash, its <code>command</code> field holds the shell command.</li>
</ul>

<span data-as="p">Your script can parse that JSON and act on any of those fields. <code>UserPromptSubmit</code> hooks get the <code>prompt</code> text instead, <code>SessionStart</code> hooks get a <code>source</code> of <code>startup</code>, <code>resume</code>, <code>clear</code>, <code>compact</code>, or <code>fork</code>, and so on. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#common-input-fields">Common input fields</a> in the reference for shared fields, and each event’s section for event-specific schemas.</span>

<span data-as="p">The exit code determines what happens next:</span>
<ul>
<li><strong>Exit 0</strong>: your hook reports no objection through its exit code.<!-- -->
<ul>
<li>For a <code>PreToolUse</code> hook this doesn’t approve the tool call: the normal <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions">permission flow</a> still applies.</li>
<li>For <code>UserPromptSubmit</code>, <code>UserPromptExpansion</code>, <code>SessionStart</code>, and <code>PostModelSwitch</code> hooks, Claude Code adds stdout it <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-0">treats as plain text</a> to Claude’s context.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Exit 2</strong>: Claude Code blocks the action. Write a reason to stderr. Where it lands depends on the event: some events feed it to Claude as feedback so it can adjust, others show it to the user, and a few, such as <code>ConfigChange</code> and <code>Elicitation</code>, surface no message. Some events can’t be blocked: for <code>SessionStart</code> and others, exit 2 shows stderr to the user and execution continues. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-2-behavior-per-event">exit code 2 behavior per event</a> for the full list.</li>
<li><strong>Any other exit code</strong>: for most events, the outcome depends on what your hook printed to stdout:<!-- -->
<ul>
<li>A parsed object that passes schema validation: Claude Code ignores the exit code, the JSON alone decides the outcome, and the hook isn’t reported as an error. The per-event exceptions, like <code>WorktreeCreate</code> failing on any nonzero exit, are listed in the reference’s <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-output">Exit code output</a> section.</li>
<li>A parsed object that fails schema validation, or stdout that Claude Code <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-0">tries to parse as JSON</a> but that isn’t valid JSON: a non-blocking error; the notice carries the validation or parse message.</li>
<li>Stdout that Claude Code <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-0">treats as plain text</a>, or empty stdout: the action proceeds as a non-blocking error. The transcript shows a <code>&lt;hook name&gt; hook error</code> notice, then the first line of stderr prefixed with <code>Failed with non-blocking status code:</code>. To capture the full stderr, enable <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#debug-hooks">debug logging</a> with <code>claude --debug</code> or by running <code>/debug</code> mid-session.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h4 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="structured-json-output"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#structured-json-output" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Structured JSON output</span></h4>
<span data-as="p">Exit codes only let you block or stay silent. For more control, exit 0 and print a JSON object to stdout instead.</span>
<div role="note" aria-label="Note" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-blue-200 bg-blue-50 dark:border-blue-900 dark:bg-blue-600/20" data-callout-type="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-4 text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300"><path d="M 9 1.6714 C 13.0371 1.6714 16.3286 4.9629 16.3286 9 C 16.3286 13.0371 13.0371 16.3286 9 16.3286 C 7.0574 16.3252 5.1953 15.552 3.8217 14.1783 C 2.448 12.8047 1.6748 10.9426 1.6714 9 C 1.6714 4.9629 4.9629 1.6714 9 1.6714 Z M 9 0 C 4.0371 0 0 4.0371 0 9 C 0 13.9629 4.0371 18 9 18 C 13.9629 18 18 13.9629 18 9 C 18 4.0371 13.9629 0 9 0 Z M 10.2857 3.8571 H 7.7143 V 10.2857 H 10.2857 V 3.8571 Z M 10.2857 11.5714 H 7.7143 V 14.1429 H 10.2857 V 11.5714 Z" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" fill-rule="evenodd" clip-rule="evenodd"></path></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">Use exit 2 to block with a stderr message, or exit 0 with JSON for structured control. Choose one approach per hook. For what happens when you mix them, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#exit-code-output">Exit code output</a>.</span></div></div>

language="json" numberOfLines="7"><span class="line"><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">{</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#116329;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">  &quot;hookSpecificOutput&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: {</span></span>

<span class="line"><span style="color:#116329;--shiki-dark:#9CDCFE">    &quot;permissionDecision&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">: </span><span style="color:#0A3069;--shiki-dark:#CE9178">&quot;deny&quot;</span><span style="color:#1F2328;--shiki-dark:#D4D4D4">,</span></span>

</code></pre></div></div></div></div><div class="code-block-fade-overlay print:hidden" data-fade-overlay="true" aria-hidden="true" style="--fade-color-light:#ffffff;--fade-color-dark:#0B0C0E"></div></div>
<span data-as="p">With <code>&quot;deny&quot;</code>, Claude Code cancels the tool call and feeds <code>permissionDecisionReason</code> back to Claude.</span>
<span data-as="p">On <code>PreToolUse</code>, Claude Code handles each <code>permissionDecision</code> value as follows:</span>
<ul>
<li><code>&quot;allow&quot;</code>: skip the interactive permission prompt. Deny and ask rules, including enterprise managed deny lists, still apply, as do prompts for MCP tools marked <a class="link" href="/docs/en/mcp#require-approval-for-a-specific-tool"><code>requiresUserInteraction</code></a> and for connector tools <a class="link" href="/docs/en/mcp#organization-controls-on-connector-tools">your organization set to <code>ask</code></a> in sessions where that setting reaches Claude Code</li>
<li><code>&quot;deny&quot;</code>: cancel the tool call and send the reason to Claude</li>
<li><code>&quot;ask&quot;</code>: show the permission prompt to the user as normal</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">A fourth value, <code>&quot;defer&quot;</code>, is available in <a class="link" href="/docs/en/headless">non-interactive mode</a> with the <code>-p</code> flag. It exits the process with the tool call preserved so an Agent SDK wrapper can collect input and resume. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#defer-a-tool-call-for-later">Defer a tool call for later</a> in the reference.</span>
<span data-as="p">A <code>PreModelSwitch</code> hook returns the same <code>permissionDecision</code> field: <code>&quot;allow&quot;</code> lets a model switch proceed, and <code>&quot;deny&quot;</code> cancels it. <code>&quot;ask&quot;</code> has you confirm the switch when you run <code>/model</code> in an interactive session; everywhere else, Claude Code treats <code>&quot;ask&quot;</code> as a refusal. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#premodelswitch-decision-control">PreModelSwitch decision control</a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">Other events use different decision patterns. For example, <code>PostToolUse</code> and <code>Stop</code> hooks use a top-level <code>decision: &quot;block&quot;</code> field, while <code>PermissionRequest</code> uses <code>hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior</code>. See the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#decision-control">summary table</a> in the reference for a full breakdown by event.</span>
<span data-as="p">For <code>UserPromptSubmit</code> hooks, use <code>hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext</code> instead to inject text into Claude’s context. Nest <code>additionalContext</code> inside <code>hookSpecificOutput</code>; if you place it at the top level of the JSON, Claude Code silently ignores it. For example, this output adds the current branch state to every prompt:</span>

<span data-as="p">The <code>&quot;Edit|Write&quot;</code> matcher fires only when Claude uses the <code>Edit</code> or <code>Write</code> tool, not when it uses <code>Bash</code>, <code>Read</code>, or any other tool. On Claude Code v2.1.191 or later, a comma separates alternatives the same way, so <code>&quot;Edit, Write&quot;</code> is equivalent. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#matcher-patterns">Matcher patterns</a> for how plain names and regular expressions are evaluated.</span>
<div role="note" aria-label="Note" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-blue-200 bg-blue-50 dark:border-blue-900 dark:bg-blue-600/20" data-callout-type="note"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-4 text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300"><path d="M 9 1.6714 C 13.0371 1.6714 16.3286 4.9629 16.3286 9 C 16.3286 13.0371 13.0371 16.3286 9 16.3286 C 7.0574 16.3252 5.1953 15.552 3.8217 14.1783 C 2.448 12.8047 1.6748 10.9426 1.6714 9 C 1.6714 4.9629 4.9629 1.6714 9 1.6714 Z M 9 0 C 4.0371 0 0 4.0371 0 9 C 0 13.9629 4.0371 18 9 18 C 13.9629 18 18 13.9629 18 9 C 18 4.0371 13.9629 0 9 0 Z M 10.2857 3.8571 H 7.7143 V 10.2857 H 10.2857 V 3.8571 Z M 10.2857 11.5714 H 7.7143 V 14.1429 H 10.2857 V 11.5714 Z" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" fill-rule="evenodd" clip-rule="evenodd"></path></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-blue-800 dark:text-blue-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">Claude can also create or modify files by running shell commands. If your hook must see every file change, such as for compliance scanning or audit logging, add a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#stop"><code>Stop</code></a> hook that scans the working tree once per turn. For per-call coverage instead, also match <code>Bash|PowerShell</code> and have your script list modified and untracked files with <code>git status --porcelain</code>. The <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#powershell">PowerShell hook input section</a> explains why matching <code>Bash</code> alone is not enough. To run a hook when a specific file changes on disk, whatever wrote it, use a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#filechanged">FileChanged</a> hook.</span></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Each event type matches on a specific field:</span>

Tools from a <a class="link" href="/docs/en/mcp#plugin-provided-mcp-servers">plugin-bundled server</a> use a scoped server segment instead, such as <code>mcp__plugin_my-plugin_db__query</code>. Use a regex matcher to target all tools from a specific server, or match across servers with a pattern like <code>mcp__.*__write.*</code>. <span data-as="p">The <code>if</code> field uses <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions">permission rule syntax</a> to filter hooks by tool name and arguments together, so the hook process only spawns when the tool call matches. This goes beyond <code>matcher</code>, which filters at the group level by tool name only.</span>
<span data-as="p">For example, this configuration runs a hook only when Claude uses <code>git</code> commands rather than all Bash commands:</span>

<span data-as="p">Whether your hook command runs depends on the shape of your <code>if</code> pattern and the Bash command Claude is invoking:</span>
<!-- --><div role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]"><div role="region" data-id="base-ui-_R_tsllktbsnlhjiuasnpfiutb_-viewport" tabindex="-1" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" style="overflow:scroll" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" aria-label="Scrollable table"><div role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" class="flex"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&amp;_td]:min-w-[150px] [&amp;_th]:text-left [&amp;_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums"><thead><tr><th style="text-align:left"><code>if</code> pattern</th><th style="text-align:left">Bash command</th><th style="text-align:left">Hook runs?</th><th style="text-align:left">Why</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>Bash(git *)</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>git push</code></td><td style="text-align:left">yes</td><td style="text-align:left">command name matches</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>Bash(git *)</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>npm test &amp;&amp; git push</code></td><td style="text-align:left">yes</td><td style="text-align:left">each subcommand is checked; <code>git push</code> matches</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>Bash(git *)</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>echo $(git log)</code></td><td style="text-align:left">yes</td><td style="text-align:left">commands inside <code>$()</code> and backticks are checked; <code>git log</code> matches</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>Bash(git *)</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>echo $(date)</code></td><td style="text-align:left">no</td><td style="text-align:left">no subcommand matches <code>git *</code></td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>Bash(git push *)</code></td><td style="text-align:left"><code>echo $(date)</code></td><td style="text-align:left">yes</td><td style="text-align:left">patterns that specify more than the command name run the hook anyway on <code>$()</code>, backticks, or <code>$VAR</code></td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">When Claude Code can’t determine which commands the Bash input runs, it runs your hook regardless of the pattern. The <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#bash-if-matching">Bash matching table</a> covers the command shapes Claude Code can and can’t narrow by subcommand. Because the filter is best-effort, use the <a class="link" href="/docs/en/permissions">permission system</a> rather than a hook to enforce a hard allow or deny.</span>
<span data-as="p">The <code>if</code> field accepts the same patterns as permission rules: <code>&quot;Bash(git *)&quot;</code>, <code>&quot;Edit(*.ts)&quot;</code>, and so on. To match multiple tool names, use separate handlers each with its own <code>if</code> value, or match at the <code>matcher</code> level where pipe alternation is supported.</span>
<span data-as="p"><code>if</code> only works on tool events: <code>PreToolUse</code>, <code>PostToolUse</code>, <code>PostToolUseFailure</code>, <code>PermissionRequest</code>, and <code>PermissionDenied</code>. Adding it to any other event prevents the hook from running.</span>
<h3 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="configure-hook-location"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#configure-hook-location" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Configure hook location</span></h3>
<span data-as="p">Where you add a hook determines its scope:</span>
<!-- --><div role="presentation" style="position:relative;--scroll-area-corner-height:0px;--scroll-area-corner-width:0px" data-component-part="scroll-area" data-table-wrapper="true" class="min-w-0 [--page-padding:20px] flex w-[calc(100%+(var(--page-padding)*2))] my-[1em] py-[1em] -mx-(--page-padding) max-w-none [contain:inline-size]"><div role="region" data-id="base-ui-_R_vcllktbsnlhjiuasnpfiutb_-viewport" tabindex="-1" class="size-full rounded-[inherit] [--scroll-area-fade-size:32px] overflow-y-hidden! base-ui-disable-scrollbar" style="overflow:scroll" data-component-part="scroll-area-viewport" aria-label="Scrollable table"><div role="presentation" style="min-width:fit-content" data-component-part="scroll-area-content" class="flex"><div class="px-(--page-padding) grow max-w-none table"><table class="m-0 min-w-full w-full max-w-none table [&amp;_td]:min-w-[150px] [&amp;_th]:text-left [&amp;_td[data-numeric]]:tabular-nums"><thead><tr><th style="text-align:left">Location</th><th style="text-align:left">Scope</th><th style="text-align:left">Shareable</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>~/.claude/settings.json</code></td><td style="text-align:left">All your projects</td><td style="text-align:left">No, local to your machine</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>.claude/settings.json</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Single project</td><td style="text-align:left">Yes, can be committed to the repo</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><code>.claude/settings.local.json</code></td><td style="text-align:left">Single project</td><td style="text-align:left">No, gitignored when Claude Code saves a setting to it</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left">Managed policy settings</td><td style="text-align:left">Organization-wide</td><td style="text-align:left">Yes, admin-controlled</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><a class="link" href="/docs/en/plugins">Plugin</a> <code>hooks/hooks.json</code></td><td style="text-align:left">When plugin is enabled</td><td style="text-align:left">Yes, bundled with the plugin</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><a class="link" href="/docs/en/skills">Skill</a> frontmatter</td><td style="text-align:left">The rest of the session once the skill is invoked. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#hooks-in-skills-and-agents">Hooks in skills and agents</a></td><td style="text-align:left">Yes, defined in the skill file</td></tr><tr><td style="text-align:left"><a class="link" href="/docs/en/sub-agents">Subagent</a> frontmatter</td><td style="text-align:left">While that subagent is running</td><td style="text-align:left">Yes, defined in the subagent file</td></tr></tbody></table></div></div></div></div>
<span data-as="p">Run <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#the-%2Fhooks-menu"><code>/hooks</code></a> in Claude Code to browse all configured hooks grouped by event.</span>
<span data-as="p">To disable hooks, set <code>&quot;disableAllHooks&quot;: true</code> in your settings file. Claude Code reads the value left after <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#disable-or-remove-hooks">settings precedence</a> applies, so a project’s settings file can override yours. Hooks configured in managed settings still run unless <code>disableAllHooks</code> is also set there. For the full reach of each level, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/settings-reference#disableallhooks"><code>disableAllHooks</code></a>.</span>
<span data-as="p">If you edit settings files directly while Claude Code is running, the file watcher normally picks up hook changes automatically.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="prompt-based-hooks"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#prompt-based-hooks" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Prompt-based hooks</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">For decisions that require judgment rather than deterministic rules, use <code>type: &quot;prompt&quot;</code> hooks. Instead of running a shell command, Claude Code sends your prompt and the hook’s input data to a Claude model, Haiku by default, to make the decision. You can specify a different model with the <code>model</code> field if you need more capability.</span>
<span data-as="p">The model’s only job is to return its decision as JSON:</span>
<ul>
<li><code>&quot;ok&quot;: true</code>: the action proceeds</li>
<li><code>&quot;ok&quot;: false</code>: what happens depends on the event:<!-- -->
<ul>
<li><code>Stop</code> and <code>SubagentStop</code>: the <code>reason</code> is fed back to Claude so it keeps working, unless the response also sets <code>&quot;impossible&quot;: true</code> to mark the condition as one that can never be satisfied, in which case Claude Code allows the stop and the turn ends</li>
<li><code>PreToolUse</code>: the tool call is denied; by default the turn ends and the deny <code>reason</code> appears in the chat as a warning line. Set <code>continueOnBlock: true</code> on the hook to instead return the <code>reason</code> to Claude as the tool error, so it can adjust and continue. Before v2.1.210, the deny <code>reason</code> was returned to Claude as the tool error and the turn continued</li>
<li><code>PostToolUse</code>: by default the turn ends and the <code>reason</code> appears in the chat as a warning line. Set <code>continueOnBlock: true</code> to feed the <code>reason</code> back to Claude and continue the turn instead</li>
<li><code>PostToolBatch</code>, <code>UserPromptSubmit</code>, and <code>UserPromptExpansion</code>: the turn ends and the <code>reason</code> appears in the chat as a warning line</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<span data-as="p">This example uses a <code>Stop</code> hook to ask the model whether all requested tasks are complete. If the model returns <code>&quot;ok&quot;: false</code> because the condition isn’t met yet, Claude keeps working and uses the <code>reason</code> as its next instruction:</span>

2.25Z" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></button></div><div class="code-block-copy-button z-10 select-none" id="base-ui-_R_1ub1kllktbsnlhjiuasnpfiutb_" <h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="agent-based-hooks"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#agent-based-hooks" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">Agent-based hooks</span></h2>
<div role="note" aria-label="Warning" class="callout my-4 px-5 py-4 overflow-hidden rounded-2xl flex gap-3 border border-yellow-200 bg-yellow-50 dark:border-yellow-900 dark:bg-yellow-600/20 [&amp;_[data-component-part=&#x27;callout-icon&#x27;]]:mt-px" data-callout-type="warning"><div class="mt-0.5 w-4" data-component-part="callout-icon"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="flex-none size-5 text-yellow-800 dark:text-yellow-300"><path d="M 9 6.75 v 1.5 m 0 3 h 0.0075 m -5.2035 3 h 10.392 c 1.155 0 1.8765 -1.2503 1.299 -2.25 L 10.299 3 c -0.5775 -0.9997 -2.0205 -0.9997 -2.598 0 L 2.505 12 c -0.5775 0.9997 0.144 2.25 1.299 2.25 z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"></path></svg></div><div class="text-sm prose dark:prose-invert min-w-0 w-full [&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-light dark:[&amp;_kbd]:bg-background-dark [&amp;_code]:text-current! [&amp;_kbd]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:text-current! [&amp;_a]:border-current [&amp;_strong]:text-current! text-yellow-800 dark:text-yellow-300" data-component-part="callout-content"><span data-as="p">Agent hooks are experimental. Behavior and configuration may change in future releases. For production workflows, prefer <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#command-hook-fields">command hooks</a>.</span></div></div>
<span data-as="p">When verification requires inspecting files or running commands, use <code>type: &quot;agent&quot;</code> hooks. Unlike prompt hooks, which make a single LLM call, agent hooks spawn a subagent that can read files, search code, and use other tools to verify conditions before returning a decision.</span>
<span data-as="p">Agent hooks use the <code>&quot;ok&quot;</code> / <code>&quot;reason&quot;</code> response format with a longer default timeout of 60 seconds and up to 50 tool-use turns. They don’t support the prompt-hook <code>impossible</code> field. On <code>ok: false</code>, Claude Code handles an agent hook the way it handles a prompt hook with <code>continueOnBlock: true</code> on the same event, so on <code>PreToolUse</code> and <code>PostToolUse</code> the turn continues; agent hooks have no <code>continueOnBlock</code> field. See <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#agent-hook-configuration">agent hook configuration</a> for the fields, including the <code>$ARGUMENTS</code> placeholder that Claude Code replaces with the hook’s JSON input.</span>
<span data-as="p">This example verifies that tests pass before allowing Claude to stop:</span>

<span data-as="p">Use prompt hooks when the hook input data alone is enough to make a decision. Use agent hooks when you need to verify something against the actual state of the codebase.</span>
<span data-as="p">For full configuration options, see <a class="link" href="/docs/en/hooks#agent-based-hooks">Agent-based hooks</a> in the reference.</span>
<h2 class="flex whitespace-pre-wrap group font-semibold" id="http-hooks"><div class="absolute" tabindex="-1"><a href="#http-hooks" class="-ml-10 flex items-center opacity-0 border-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus:opacity-100 focus:outline-0 group/link" aria-label="Navigate to header">​<div class="size-6 rounded-md flex items-center justify-center shadow-xs text-gray-400 dark:text-white/50 dark:bg-background-dark dark:brightness-[1.35] dark:ring-1 dark:hover:brightness-150 bg-white ring-1 ring-gray-400/30 dark:ring-gray-700/25 hover:ring-gray-400/60 dark:hover:ring-white/20 group-focus/link:border-2 group-focus/link:border-primary dark:group-focus/link:border-primary-light"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" class="size-3 shrink-0"><path d="M8.50001 6.827C8.14801 6.995 7.81801 7.225 7.52701 7.517L7.51701 7.527C6.13601 8.908 6.13601 11.146 7.51701 12.527L9.69201 14.702C11.073 16.083 13.311 16.083 14.692 14.702L14.702 14.692C16.083 13.311 16.083 11.073 14.702 9.692L13.771 8.761" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path><path d="M9.50002 11.173C9.85202 11.005 10.182 10.775 10.473 10.483L10.483 10.473C11.864 9.092 11.864 6.854 10.483 5.473L8.30802 3.298C6.92702 1.917 4.68902 1.917 3.30802 3.298L3.29802 3.308C1.91702 4.689 1.91702 6.927 3.29802 8.308L4.22902 9.239" stroke="currentColor" width="1.5" linecap="round" linejoin="round"></path></svg></div></a></div><span class="cursor-pointer">HTTP hooks</span></h2>
<span data-as="p">Use <code>type: &quot;http&quot;</code> hooks to POST event data to an HTTP endpoint instead of running a shell command. The endpoint receives the same JSON that a command hook would receive on stdin, and returns results through the HTTP response body using the same JSON format.</span>
<span data-as="p">HTTP hooks are useful when you want a web server, cloud function, or external service to handle hook logic: for example, a shared audit service that logs tool use events across a team.</span>
<span data-as="p">This example posts every tool use to a local logging service:</span>
